disposition_reason: Experimental study that spiked buffalo milk with 1 ppm lead acetate or cadmium chloride before making caciotta cheese and measured oxidative and antioxidant markers; no lead or cadmium concentrations in milk or cheese are reported.

study.design: controlled spiking experiment (control, Pb 1 ppm, Cd 1 ppm milk batches; n = 10 cheeses per batch)
study.origin: buffalo farm, province of Potenza, Basilicata, Italy
study.market: bulk milk bought from a supermarket in Potenza
study.method: metal analysis method not described; outcomes are composition, PV, ADV, TBARs, fatty acids, ABTS, FRAP, thiols, SOD

unresolved: Authors state preliminary determinations on the bulk milk were below the detection limit, but give no method, LOD or values; not recorded as a finding.
Spiked cheeses are experimental and never occurrence data.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU Regulations 2021/1323 and 2021/1317 quoted: Cd 0.005 mg/kg and Pb 0.020 mg/kg for milk and cow-milk-protein products; EFSA Cd TWI 2.5 µg/kg bw, Pb BMDL01 0.5-1.5 µg/kg bw/day
